paragraphs.text: Now I make known unto you brethren, the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye received, wherein also ye stand,
paragraphs.original: Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, ὃ καὶ παρελάβετε, ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἑστήκατε,
paragraphs.translit: Gnōrizō de hymin, adelphoi, to euangelion ho euēngelisamēn hymin, ho kai parelabete, en hō kai hestēkate,

paragraphs.text: by which also ye are saved, if ye hold fast the word which I preached unto you, except ye believed in vain.
paragraphs.original: διʼ οὗ καὶ σῴζεσθε, τίνι λόγῳ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν, εἰ κατέχετε, ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε.
paragraphs.translit: diʼ hou kai sōzesthe, tini logō euēngelisamēn hymin, ei katechete, ektos ei mē eikē episteusate.

paragraphs.text: For I delivered unto you first of all that which also I received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;
paragraphs.original: Παρέδωκα γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν πρώτοις, ὃ καὶ παρέλαβον, ὅτι Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
paragraphs.translit: Paredōka gar hymin en prōtois, ho kai parelabon, hoti Christos apethanen hyper tōn hamartiōn hēmōn kata tas graphas,

paragraphs.text: and that he was buried; and that he hath been raised on the third day according to the scriptures;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτι ἐτάφη, καὶ ὅτι ἐγήγερται τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ κατὰ τὰς γραφάς,
paragraphs.translit: kai hoti etaphē, kai hoti egēgertai tē hēmera tē tritē kata tas graphas,

paragraphs.text: and that he appeared to Cephas; then to the twelve;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτι ὤφθη Κηφᾷ, εἶτα τοῖς δώδεκα·
paragraphs.translit: kai hoti ōphthē Kēpha, eita tois dōdeka·

paragraphs.text: then he appeared to above five hundred brethren at once, of whom the greater part remain until now, but some are fallen asleep;
paragraphs.original: ἔπειτα ὤφθη ἐπάνω πεντακοσίοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐφάπαξ, ἐξ ὧν οἱ πλείονες μένουσιν ἕως ἄρτι, τινὲς δὲ ἐκοιμήθησαν·
paragraphs.translit: epeita ōphthē epanō pentakosiois adelphois ephapax, ex hōn hoi pleiones menousin heōs arti, tines de ekoimēthēsan·

paragraphs.text: then he appeared to James; then to all the apostles;
paragraphs.original: ἔπειτα ὤφθη Ἰακώβῳ, εἶτα τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πᾶσιν·
paragraphs.translit: epeita ōphthē Iakōbō, eita tois apostolois pasin·

paragraphs.text: and last of all, as to the [child] untimely born, he appeared to me also.
paragraphs.original: ἔσχατον δὲ πάντων ὡσπερεὶ τῷ ἐκτρώματι ὤφθη κἀμοί.
paragraphs.translit: eschaton de pantōn hōsperei tō ektrōmati ōphthē kamoi.

paragraphs.text: For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ἐλάχιστος τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὃς οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς καλεῖσθαι ἀπόστολος, διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: egō gar eimi ho elachistos tōn apostolōn, hos ouk eimi hikanos kaleisthai apostolos, dioti ediōxa tēn ekklēsian tou theou·

paragraphs.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not found vain; but I labored more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
paragraphs.original: χάριτι δὲ θεοῦ εἰμι ὅ εἰμι, καὶ ἡ χάρις αὐτοῦ ἡ εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη, ἀλλὰ περισσότερον αὐτῶν πάντων ἐκοπίασα, οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλὰ ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ σὺν ἐμοί.
paragraphs.translit: chariti de theou eimi ho eimi, kai hē charis autou hē eis eme ou kenē egenēthē, alla perissoteron autōn pantōn ekopiasa, ouk egō de alla hē charis tou theou hē syn emoi.

paragraphs.text: Whether then [it be] I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.
paragraphs.original: εἴτε οὖν ἐγὼ εἴτε ἐκεῖνοι, οὕτως κηρύσσομεν καὶ οὕτως ἐπιστεύσατε.
paragraphs.translit: eite oun egō eite ekeinoi, houtōs kēryssomen kai houtōs episteusate.

paragraphs.text: Now if Christ is preached that he hath been raised from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς κηρύσσεται ὅτι ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγήγερται, πῶς λέγουσιν ἐν ὑμῖν τινες ὅτι ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν;
paragraphs.translit: Ei de Christos kēryssetai hoti ek nekrōn egēgertai, pōs legousin en hymin tines hoti anastasis nekrōn ouk estin;

paragraphs.text: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither hath Christ been raised:
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
paragraphs.translit: ei de anastasis nekrōn ouk estin, oude Christos egēgertai·

paragraphs.text: and if Christ hath not been raised, then is our preaching vain, your faith also is vain.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, κενὸν ἄρα τὸ κήρυγμα ἡμῶν, κενὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν,
paragraphs.translit: ei de Christos ouk egēgertai, kenon ara to kērygma hēmōn, kenē kai hē pistis hymōn,

paragraphs.text: Yea, we are found false witnesses of God; because we witnessed of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead are not raised.
paragraphs.original: εὑρισκόμεθα δὲ καὶ ψευδομάρτυρες τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ἐμαρτυρήσαμεν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι ἤγειρεν τὸν Χριστόν, ὃν οὐκ ἤγειρεν εἴπερ ἄρα νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται.
paragraphs.translit: heuriskometha de kai pseudomartyres tou theou, hoti emartyrēsamen kata tou theou hoti ēgeiren ton Christon, hon ouk ēgeiren eiper ara nekroi ouk egeirontai.

paragraphs.text: For if the dead are not raised, neither hath Christ been raised:
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται·
paragraphs.translit: ei gar nekroi ouk egeirontai, oude Christos egēgertai·

paragraphs.text: and if Christ hath not been raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται, ματαία ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν, ἔτι ἐστὲ ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ei de Christos ouk egēgertai, mataia hē pistis hymōn, eti este en tais hamartiais hymōn.

paragraphs.text: Then they also that are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
paragraphs.original: ἄρα καὶ οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο.
paragraphs.translit: ara kai hoi koimēthentes en Christō apōlonto.

paragraphs.text: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.
paragraphs.original: εἰ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ ἐν Χριστῷ ἠλπικότες ἐσμὲν μόνον, ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐσμέν.
paragraphs.translit: ei en tē zōē tautē en Christō ēlpikotes esmen monon, eleeinoteroi pantōn anthrōpōn esmen.

paragraphs.text: But now hath Christ been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of them that are asleep.
paragraphs.original: Νυνὶ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων.
paragraphs.translit: Nyni de Christos egēgertai ek nekrōn, aparchē tōn kekoimēmenōn.

paragraphs.text: For since by man [came] death, by man [came] also the resurrection of the dead.
paragraphs.original: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ διʼ ἀνθρώπου θάνατος, καὶ διʼ ἀνθρώπου ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν·
paragraphs.translit: epeidē gar diʼ anthrōpou thanatos, kai diʼ anthrōpou anastasis nekrōn·

paragraphs.text: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ shall all be made alive.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πάντες ἀποθνῄσκουσιν, οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ πάντες ζῳοποιηθήσονται.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar en tō Adam pantes apothnēskousin, houtōs kai en tō Christō pantes zōopoiēthēsontai.

paragraphs.text: But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; then they that are Christ`s, at his coming.
paragraphs.original: ἕκαστος δὲ ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι· ἀπαρχὴ Χριστός, ἔπειτα οἱ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hekastos de en tō idiō tagmati· aparchē Christos, epeita hoi tou Christou en tē parousia autou·

paragraphs.text: Then [cometh] the end, when he shall deliver up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have abolished all rule and all authority and power.
paragraphs.original: εἶτα τὸ τέλος, ὅταν παραδιδῷ τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί, ὅταν καταργήσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρχὴν καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξουσίαν καὶ δύναμιν,
paragraphs.translit: eita to telos, hotan paradidō tēn basileian tō theō kai patri, hotan katargēsē pasan archēn kai pasan exousian kai dynamin,

paragraphs.text: For he must reign, till he hath put all his enemies under his feet.
paragraphs.original: δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἄχρι οὗ θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: dei gar auton basileuein achri hou thē pantas tous echthrous hypo tous podas autou.

paragraphs.text: The last enemy that shall be abolished is death.
paragraphs.original: ἔσχατος ἐχθρὸς καταργεῖται ὁ θάνατος,
paragraphs.translit: eschatos echthros katargeitai ho thanatos,

paragraphs.text: For, He put all things in subjection under his feet. But when he saith, All things are put in subjection, it is evident that he is excepted who did subject all things unto him.
paragraphs.original: πάντα γὰρ ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ. ὅταν δὲ εἴπῃ ὅτι πάντα ὑποτέτακται, δῆλον ὅτι ἐκτὸς τοῦ ὑποτάξαντος αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα.
paragraphs.translit: panta gar hypetaxen hypo tous podas autou. hotan de eipē hoti panta hypotetaktai, dēlon hoti ektos tou hypotaxantos autō ta panta.

paragraphs.text: And when all things have been subjected unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subjected to him that did subject all things unto him, that God may be all in all.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ ὑποταγῇ αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, τότε αὐτὸς ὁ υἱὸς ὑποταγήσεται τῷ ὑποτάξαντι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα, ἵνα ᾖ ὁ θεὸς πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de hypotagē autō ta panta, tote autos ho hyios hypotagēsetai tō hypotaxanti autō ta panta, hina ē ho theos panta en pasin.

paragraphs.text: Else what shall they do that are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized for them?
paragraphs.original: Ἐπεὶ τί ποιήσουσιν οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν; εἰ ὅλως νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, τί καὶ βαπτίζονται ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν;
paragraphs.translit: Epei ti poiēsousin hoi baptizomenoi hyper tōn nekrōn; ei holōs nekroi ouk egeirontai, ti kai baptizontai hyper autōn;

paragraphs.text: Why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?
paragraphs.original: τί καὶ ἡμεῖς κινδυνεύομεν πᾶσαν ὥραν;
paragraphs.translit: ti kai hēmeis kindyneuomen pasan hōran;

paragraphs.text: I protest by that glorifying in you, brethren, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.
paragraphs.original: καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀποθνῄσκω, νὴ τὴν ὑμετέραν καύχησιν, ἣν ἔχω ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kathʼ hēmeran apothnēskō, nē tēn hymeteran kauchēsin, hēn echō en Christō Iēsou tō kyriō hēmōn.

paragraphs.text: If after the manner of men I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what doth it profit me? If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die.
paragraphs.original: εἰ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, τί μοι τὸ ὄφελος; εἰ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται, Φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν, αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκομεν.
paragraphs.translit: ei kata anthrōpon ethēriomachēsa en Ephesō, ti moi to ophelos; ei nekroi ouk egeirontai, Phagōmen kai piōmen, aurion gar apothnēskomen.

paragraphs.text: Be not deceived: Evil companionships corrupt good morals.
paragraphs.original: μὴ πλανᾶσθε· φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρηστὰ ὁμιλίαι κακαί.
paragraphs.translit: mē planasthe· phtheirousin ēthē chrēsta homiliai kakai.

paragraphs.text: Awake to soberness righteously, and sin not; for some have no knowledge of God: I speak [this] to move you to shame.
paragraphs.original: ἐκνήψατε δικαίως καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε, ἀγνωσίαν γὰρ θεοῦ τινες ἔχουσιν· πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λαλῶ.
paragraphs.translit: eknēpsate dikaiōs kai mē hamartanete, agnōsian gar theou tines echousin· pros entropēn hymin lalō.

paragraphs.text: But some one will say, How are the dead raised? and with what manner of body do they come?
paragraphs.original: Ἀλλὰ ἐρεῖ τις· Πῶς ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροί, ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται;
paragraphs.translit: Alla erei tis· Pōs egeirontai hoi nekroi, poiō de sōmati erchontai;

paragraphs.text: Thou foolish one, that which thou thyself sowest is not quickened except it die:
paragraphs.original: ἄφρων, σὺ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ ζῳοποιεῖται ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·
paragraphs.translit: aphrōn, sy ho speireis, ou zōopoieitai ean mē apothanē·

paragraphs.text: and that which thou sowest, thou sowest not the body that shall be, but a bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other kind;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ τὸ σῶμα τὸ γενησόμενον σπείρεις ἀλλὰ γυμνὸν κόκκον εἰ τύχοι σίτου ἤ τινος τῶν λοιπῶν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ho speireis, ou to sōma to genēsomenon speireis alla gymnon kokkon ei tychoi sitou ē tinos tōn loipōn·

paragraphs.text: but God giveth it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς δίδωσιν αὐτῷ σῶμα καθὼς ἠθέλησεν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν σπερμάτων ἴδιον σῶμα.
paragraphs.translit: ho de theos didōsin autō sōma kathōs ēthelēsen, kai hekastō tōn spermatōn idion sōma.

paragraphs.text: All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one [flesh] of men, and another flesh of beasts, and another flesh of birds, and another of fishes.
paragraphs.original: οὐ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἡ αὐτὴ σάρξ, ἀλλὰ ἄλλη μὲν ἀνθρώπων, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ πτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ ἰχθύων.
paragraphs.translit: ou pasa sarx hē autē sarx, alla allē men anthrōpōn, allē de sarx ktēnōn, allē de sarx ptēnōn, allē de ichthyōn.

paragraphs.text: There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the [glory] of the terrestrial is another.
paragraphs.original: καὶ σώματα ἐπουράνια, καὶ σώματα ἐπίγεια· ἀλλὰ ἑτέρα μὲν ἡ τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξα, ἑτέρα δὲ ἡ τῶν ἐπιγείων.
paragraphs.translit: kai sōmata epourania, kai sōmata epigeia· alla hetera men hē tōn epouraniōn doxa, hetera de hē tōn epigeiōn.

paragraphs.text: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differeth from another star in glory.
paragraphs.original: ἄλλη δόξα ἡλίου, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα σελήνης, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα ἀστέρων, ἀστὴρ γὰρ ἀστέρος διαφέρει ἐν δόξῃ.
paragraphs.translit: allē doxa hēliou, kai allē doxa selēnēs, kai allē doxa asterōn, astēr gar asteros diapherei en doxē.

paragraphs.text: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:
paragraphs.original: Οὕτως καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τῶν νεκρῶν. σπείρεται ἐν φθορᾷ, ἐγείρεται ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ·
paragraphs.translit: Houtōs kai hē anastasis tōn nekrōn. speiretai en phthora, egeiretai en aphtharsia·

paragraphs.text: it is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:
paragraphs.original: σπείρεται ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δόξῃ· σπείρεται ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δυνάμει·
paragraphs.translit: speiretai en atimia, egeiretai en doxē· speiretai en astheneia, egeiretai en dynamei·

paragraphs.text: it is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual [body].
paragraphs.original: σπείρεται σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἐγείρεται σῶμα πνευματικόν. Εἰ ἔστιν σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἔστιν καὶ πνευματικόν.
paragraphs.translit: speiretai sōma psychikon, egeiretai sōma pneumatikon. Ei estin sōma psychikon, estin kai pneumatikon.

paragraphs.text: So also it is written, The first man Adam became a living soul. The last Adam [became] a life-giving spirit.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως καὶ γέγραπται· Ἐγένετο ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδὰμ εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν· ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ εἰς πνεῦμα ζῳοποιοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs kai gegraptai· Egeneto ho prōtos anthrōpos Adam eis psychēn zōsan· ho eschatos Adam eis pneuma zōopoioun.

paragraphs.text: Howbeit that is not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; then that which is spiritual.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλʼ οὐ πρῶτον τὸ πνευματικὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ψυχικόν, ἔπειτα τὸ πνευματικόν.
paragraphs.translit: allʼ ou prōton to pneumatikon alla to psychikon, epeita to pneumatikon.

paragraphs.text: The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is of heaven.
paragraphs.original: ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος ἐκ γῆς χοϊκός, ὁ δεύτερος ἄνθρωπος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho prōtos anthrōpos ek gēs choikos, ho deuteros anthrōpos ex ouranou.

paragraphs.text: As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.
paragraphs.original: οἷος ὁ χοϊκός, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί, καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι·
paragraphs.translit: hoios ho choikos, toioutoi kai hoi choikoi, kai hoios ho epouranios, toioutoi kai hoi epouranioi·

paragraphs.text: And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ, φορέσομεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου.
paragraphs.translit: kai kathōs ephoresamen tēn eikona tou choikou, phoresomen kai tēn eikona tou epouraniou.

paragraphs.text: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption.
paragraphs.original: Τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομῆσαι οὐ δύναται, οὐδὲ ἡ φθορὰ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν κληρονομεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: Touto de phēmi, adelphoi, hoti sarx kai haima basileian theou klēronomēsai ou dynatai, oude hē phthora tēn aphtharsian klēronomei.

paragraphs.text: Behold, I tell you a mystery: We all shall not sleep, but we shall all be changed,
paragraphs.original: ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα,
paragraphs.translit: idou mystērion hymin legō· pantes ou koimēthēsometha pantes de allagēsometha,

paragraphs.text: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
paragraphs.original: ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γάρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.
paragraphs.translit: en atomō, en rhipē ophthalmou, en tē eschatē salpingi· salpisei gar, kai hoi nekroi egerthēsontai aphthartoi, kai hēmeis allagēsometha.

paragraphs.text: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
paragraphs.original: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν.
paragraphs.translit: dei gar to phtharton touto endysasthai aphtharsian kai to thnēton touto endysasthai athanasian.

paragraphs.text: But when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall come to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.
paragraphs.original: ὅταν δὲ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀθανασίαν, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος· Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος.
paragraphs.translit: hotan de to phtharton touto endysētai aphtharsian kai to thnēton touto endysētai athanasian, tote genēsetai ho logos ho gegrammenos· Katepothē ho thanatos eis nikos.

paragraphs.text: O death, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?
paragraphs.original: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ νῖκος; ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον;
paragraphs.translit: pou sou, thanate, to nikos; pou sou, thanate, to kentron;

paragraphs.text: The sting of death is sin; and the power of sin is the law:
paragraphs.original: τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος·
paragraphs.translit: to de kentron tou thanatou hē hamartia, hē de dynamis tēs hamartias ho nomos·

paragraphs.text: but thanks be to God, who giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.original: τῷ δὲ θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tō de theō charis tō didonti hēmin to nikos dia tou kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labor is not vain in the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί, ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε, ἀμετακίνητοι, περισσεύοντες ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ τοῦ κυρίου πάντοτε, εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κόπος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔστιν κενὸς ἐν κυρίῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Hōste, adelphoi mou agapētoi, hedraioi ginesthe, ametakinētoi, perisseuontes en tō ergō tou kyriou pantote, eidotes hoti ho kopos hymōn ouk estin kenos en kyriō.
